subject.title: feat: per-job elevated exec scoping for cron and heartbeat

question: Should elevated cron and heartbeat execution be solved as a narrow per-job/heartbeat elevated marker, or folded into a broader Gateway-owned schedule and execution provenance model?
rationale: The remaining work changes host-exec authority and upgrade behavior, so automation should not choose the permanent trust model without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Fold Into Provenance Design
options.body: Use this issue as the elevated-exec slice of the broader non-forgeable schedule and execution provenance model, with heartbeat covered explicitly.

options.title: Implement Narrow Elevated Markers
options.body: Add per-job and heartbeat elevated authority fields now, but require explicit create, update, execution audit, and migration semantics.

options.title: Document Wildcard Risk Temporarily
options.body: Defer implementation while preserving existing trusted unattended workflows and documenting the current risk and workaround limits.

recommendation.title: Fold Into Provenance Design
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the elevated-exec slice of the broader non-forgeable schedule and execution provenance model, with heartbeat covered explicitly.

likelyOwner.reason: The closest current-main feature history is the merged agent cron caller-scope security boundary in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96883.
